lines.description: N-S central passage between the two blocks of the building, seen as a pale band; a modern walkway now runs along it
N-S line along the inner side of the eastern block (dark interior band)
E-W southern edge of the eastern block
long, sharply defined N-S double line east of the conserved buildings south-east of the 'granary'; its uniformity suggests it may be a modern conservation or boundary wall

location.basis: Centre of our z18 mosaic. We placed it from the published site position (about 30.631 N, 72.864 E) and the imagery, which shows the wooded archaeological reserve south-west of the modern town of Harappa with the conserved 'granary' of Mound F at 30.63344 N, 72.86166 E.

systems.part: Mound F, south-east of the 'granary' (uncertain date)

main_system_reason: The conserved 'granary' on Mound F is the only Harappan building whose walls stay visible over more than 20 m on the imagery; sys1 is the set of its outer and inner wall lines. We cannot see the plan of the citadel (Mound AB) or the lower town (Mounds E and ET), so sys1 stands for the town only as far as Mound F follows the same layout.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic of 23 May 2025 with real detail to zoom 18 (0.51 m per pixel). Most of Harappa is backfilled or under trees and scrub: the mounds show as a wooded reserve criss-crossed by visitor paths, and we found no wall lines on Mound AB, on Mounds E and ET or in the lower town. Two fenced rectangular areas in the centre of the site, east of Mound AB, hold faint wall traces whose lines we could not follow over 20 m, and their rectangular frames are modern protective walls or trench edges, so we did not measure them. The 'granary' on Mound F is conserved with brick capping; its walls are faint, and we measured four of its lines, raising the endpoint uncertainty to 1.2-2 px to match the faintness. To check that our readings were not pulled towards the pixel grid on which we drew the provisional lines, we re-ran three strips with a provisional end deliberately moved by 3 px and recovered the same edge positions within 0.7 px. HN1 is a sharp double line about 70 m long south-east of the 'granary'; it may be a brick drain or wall of the Harappan period, but its perfect uniformity also fits a modern conservation or boundary wall, so we report it separately and do not use it for the main system.
